fighter.about: One fighter, flown (src/carrier/fighter.mjs): the same thruster physics as the carrier, in the fighter's own frame. Built for vacuum (tools/blender/fighter_build.py): a crew capsule, two propellant tanks, radiators that fold up instead of wings; `size` is her box without the radiators, which weigh little. 12 t; the main drive gives about 3 g, the manoeuvring clusters about 1 g sideways and a 180° turn in about 2 s. `thrusters` places the Blender model's thruster quads and the main drive's force; how she actually flies (the nozzles that push, the tanks, the attitude hold) is `flight`. `landing.lane`: how far out the approach lane's rings run; `ring` their radius; `catch` how close to the gate (m along, m off the line sideways and up) and how slow (m/s) flight control catches a fighter you fly in yourself.

g.about: What g does to the pilot (src/carrier/gload.mjs). Shift with W is hard burn: the drive's push rises to `boost` times its rating over `spool` seconds, burning propellant to match. Past `tolerate` g the pilot's strain builds at `onset` a second for every g over (times `juiceCut` while the couch's `juice` lasts, seconds of it, topped up on the pad); at 1 she blacks out until it falls back under 0.45; under `tolerate` it falls at `recover` a second.

flight.about: How she flies (src/carrier/flight.mjs), as signed off in the Fighter Sound Lab: Newton only, no drag, no top speed, no drift kill. `hold`: the drive lights at `rampFrom` of full power and ramps at `rampRate` a second while W is held; the aim may lead the nose by `lead` rad; `sens` rad a mouse pixel; `keyRate` / `rollRate` the turn the arrows and Z C ask for (rad/s); `wmax` the hold's cruise turn rate per axis (pitch, yaw, roll); `minPop` the smallest pop as a fraction of a second of full jets; `gap` the beat between pops. `inertia` (kg m²) and `com` in her model's frame. `blocks`: the four jet blocks (bow and stern at the height of the centre of mass, so a slide is a pure slide and a yaw a pure yaw), `pan` for the sound. `nozzles`: [id, block, the way the gas goes, `force` kind, metres out from the block]. `alloc`: per command (slide right, rise, back (retro), pitch up, yaw left, roll left) the nozzles each way. `opposed`: pairs that would cancel, so neither opens. `tank` kg and `isp` s: 3 t of torch-drive propellant and 1.2 t of cold gas (about 250 m/s of sliding). `nozzle`: the drive's mouth.

damage.about: Her parts and what a hit on each does (src/carrier/fighter-damage.mjs). `parts`: each `id`, `name` (the cockpit's damage page), `short`, `does` (what it is), `hp` (its share of `weapons.fighter.hull`; the shares are scaled to add up to it) and `shapes` in her frame (`box` [cx, cy, cz, hx, hy, hz], `ball` [x, y, z, r], `cyl` [x, y, z0, z1, r] along z). A shot is placed on the first part its line meets (nearest the line if none), and what that part cannot take goes `pass` of it on to the next part along the line. A missile's burst gives `blast` of it to the part nearest the burst and the rest (and what that part could not take) to every part by its share and its distance (`reach` m); a crash gives `crash` of it to the part it struck and the rest to every part by its share; what a part cannot take of that share is lost. A part with `armour` takes that fraction of what reaches it (the cockpit is an armoured capsule). `guns.fhull` is the sum of the parts. She is dead in space when the cockpit is gone, the sum is gone, or the drive and `dead.jets` of the jet blocks are out. `drive`: thrust is `floor` + her health of full (nothing at 0). `radiator`: each lost one takes `drive` of the drive's full push (no waste heat shed, no full power). `jets`: a block's nozzles push at its health, nothing at 0. `tank`: a shot or a burst that does it `hole` or more holes it (a crash's shock through her does not; the part it strikes can be holed), and a hole leaks `leak[tank].rate` kg/s × the damage, and the leaking gas pushes her at `leak[tank].ve` m/s out of the hole. `guns`: under `one` one barrel fires at half the rate, under `jam` both are jammed. `cockpit`: under `crack` the canopy is cracked and the HUD flickers. `decals`: at most that many scorch marks and holes drawn on her.

repair.about: Mending a damaged fighter on her pad (src/carrier/fighter-repair.mjs). Each damaged part is one job: `min` s plus `per[does]` s for a part from nothing to whole, times what it has lost, plus `hole` s for each hole in a tank (plated and welded before the rest of the tank's work). The deck crew do what is `inside` (in her open frame, from foot restraints by her flank), the drones the rest (plates and welding, outside); each takes the waiting job first in `order`, the most damaged first within a kind. She cannot launch until every job is done. `help` is what your welding adds to a drone job (a drone is 1); you can weld a part within `reach` m of your eye. `drones`: `racks` on the hangar's walls (`at` [x, y above the floor, z] the first slot, `n` slots `gap` m apart along z, `into` the way out of the wall), flown weightless and Newtonian: up to the `lane` (m above the floor, over everything) and along it, down to a point `standoff` m off the part, at up to `cruise` m/s and `accel` m/s², steering with time constant `tau`; `radius` is the clearance they keep from the gangway and the fighters. `crew`: their `posts` on the gangway [x, z] where they wait, `speed` (m/s along their way, for the timing: they push off and glide), `setup` s at the job before the work starts, the foot restraint's height `h` and how far off her flank they stand (`flank`). `board`: the pad's board (width and height, m).
